notes:

Built-in claims classified (all non-blocking):
1. Rejected. `version-control.md:14-15` says the claim is stale, but head has the ownership-first order in `version-control.md`, `requirements.md` R-STATE, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/usage.md` and `dist/agents/holyagent.md:123`. The instruction edits arrive through the merged instruction branch (be35f58), which is outside the range the tool diffed.
2. Rejected, same reason: `requirements.md` R-STATE at head already lists the ownership-first order.
3. Optional, `packages/runtime/src/state/tree.ts:258` (the `legacy` heuristic). When `holyagent.stateMode` was set to `local` by hand with a user-written `/.holyagent/` line, leaving `local` deletes that line. The probe confirmed it and a test enshrines it. It is the deliberate trade-off for lines from the earlier unreleased build, and the command path writes the keep note. Fix if wanted: have `ensureExcluded` write the note when it sees an unmarked line.
4. Optional, `tree.ts:1000` (`setStateMode`). A failure in `unexcludeState` after the mode write reports an error although the mode has changed. The base had the same order, so it is a baseline. A retry converges for the marked-pair case.
5. Optional, `tree.ts:178`. A user line added after entering `local`, with no note recorded, is removed when leaving `local`. This is the same class as claim 3.
6. Optional, `packages/runtime/src/vcs/commit.ts:207`. The new check refuses a `local` commit only when state files are staged. The invariant still holds: commit paths must be explicit, portable and not under `.holyagent/` in `local`, `.` is rejected, and `StagedOutsideScope` catches anything else staged. The error text "git tracks files under .holyagent/ that are staged" is a bit imprecise for force-added untracked files, which is cosmetic.
7. Optional, `commit.ts:183`. With `core.ignorecase` on and an index path cased `.HolyAgent/x` in `work` mode, `inScope` compares case-sensitively. This only matters for a state folder tracked under another spelling.
8. Rejected for `editExclude` (a writer that does not hold the lock). The lock covers only holyagent commands, which is inherent to any lock on a file git and editors also write. The symlink part did not reproduce.
9. Rejected for the CRLF and trailing-newline claim. Git strips the trailing CR from exclude patterns, existing lines are preserved, and the newline policy applies only to a file that is edited.
